top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria. On public knowledge, his voice is hard to attribute to a predecessor. The Blinding trilogy and Solenoid read to me as one cumulative project that recasts memory, the body, dream and cosmology, rather than a single large effort. Attribution is clean: one author, one language, and a citation limited to the major prose with the poetry named only as its source. The main reservations are unresolved. I cannot judge the Romanian sentence directly, and I cannot confirm from public knowledge that the late, very long books extend the project rather than merely enlarge it. This is a reading, not a verified close reading. I rank Zurita (P003) second because the poems-only citation Olsson clarified removes most of my boundary objection and his formal conception is a serious challenge to the originality of Cărtărescu's form. My coverage of the poetry is thin and poetry loses the most in translation, so I cannot place him first. Can Xue (P002) is third because I cannot show development across her partly translated corpus. That limits my confidence and is not a finding that her method has hardened. I place Michon (P004) fourth because I weigh breadth across the whole oeuvre more heavily, not because his sentence is weaker. I treat that as a difference of weighting, not of merit. P000 is last because each of the four named candidates has a substantive literary case. I do not rely on support counts, fame, translation reception or national symbolism.
recusal_note: None apparent from the profile, which records no tie to any shortlisted writer. It records ordinary collegial and professional ties to the chair Anders Olsson, to Steve Sem-Sandberg (elected alongside her in 2020) and to predecessor Mats Malm. Her own non-fiction practice and her role as Permanent Secretary are context only. Her committee voting status is undocumented, and her simulated vote is a modeling assumption. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
